purpose: systems feasibility, not benchmark -- no model-quality claim should be read from this file

config.name: rgcn-base
config.mode: eval, torch.no_grad(), no backward, no optimizer

scoring_microprofile.disease_ids_used: validation-split disease IDs only (loaded.val_disease_ids), never locked-test disease IDs
scoring_microprofile.note: The encoder ran exactly once (to produce the full-graph embeddings used above); scoring both the single-disease and five-disease runs reused those same fixed embeddings with zero additional encoder forward calls, confirming the existing evaluation-harness pattern (one encoder forward per evaluation run, decoder-only scoring per disease) is directly compatible with this score_fn.

feasibility_decision.reason: Full-graph, no-grad, eval-mode encoder inference over the complete 16,195,596-edge real message-passing graph completed in well under one second (0.32s graph construction + 0.58s encoder forward), using 2,836 MB of 14,941 MB GPU memory (19.0% of the T4's reserved-memory capacity) -- comfortable headroom. The subsequent full-universe scoring micro-profile (one disease and five diseases, each against the full 7,957-drug universe) ran in single-digit milliseconds with zero extra encoder calls. No redesign toward sampled/approximate inference is needed.

next_step_note: Inference is feasible as-is; no sampled-inference strategy needs to be designed. The remaining blocker to a real validation search is purely the sampled-training neighbor-sampling throughput measured in rgcn_sampled_training_profile_e79d3e4.json, not inference.
